gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each candidate NAS costs to run per year. At a stated duty cycle (8 h drive access plus 16 h drive hibernation a day) and the August 2026 US average home electricity price of 18.16 ¢/kWh, the yearly cost is about $33 for the Synology DS925+, $38 for the DS1525+, $42 for the UGREEN DXP4800 Plus and $44 for the QNAP TS-464.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited rival pages and our own page. Camera Lookout (cited) lists access and hibernation watts for the DS925+, DXP4800 Plus and TS-464, but it says outright that electricity cost can't be calculated and gives no duty cycle or rate. Fstoppers (cited) gives no wattage at all. Our current dealectric page says it has no power figures. Adobe's pages say nothing about power. Hours to copy 10 TB over 2.5GbE and 10GbE are already on our page and in Camera Lookout's per-TB arithmetic, so throughput math would not stand out.
decides: It backs the DXP4800 Plus as the pick rather than changing it. The only 4-bay candidate with built-in 10GbE costs about $8.50 a year more to run than the DS925+, which cannot add 10GbE at all. That is about $42 over five years, so power is not a reason to choose the Synology. The QNAP TS-464 costs the most to run of the four, because its disk-standby draw of 21.6 W is the highest. It also still needs a 10GbE card to match the UGREEN. A second derived point is worth stating: Synology's headline 565 MB/s write for the DS925+ is more than one 2.5GbE port can carry (312.5 MB/s raw). So a single editing computer on one cable stays at or below 312.5 MB/s, which means at least 8.9 h to load 10 TB. Camera Lookout quotes the 565 MB/s figure without saying this.
